plan: Given my value of $36, I need to bid strategically to maximize profit. Since I pay the second-highest bid, I want to bid high enough to win against other rational bidders, but not so high that my profit is minimized if I win. A common strategy in this type of auction is to bid your true value or slightly below to ensure a positive profit if you win. With only one round and no history, I will bid my true value to maximize my chances of winning when it's profitable.

I will bid slightly above what I anticipate the second-highest bid to be, aiming to win while minimizing my payment. Given my value of $33, I will bid $32.9. This is a common strategy in a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value or slightly below is optimal to maximize profit.

[ This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with a second-price payment rule (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding below your value risks losing to a bid lower than your value, while bidding above your value risks winning and paying more than your value. Since this is the first round and there's no history to learn from, and given the nature of the auction, I will bid my true value. ]
